matchupAnalysis: Lerryan Douglas 57.9% / Jamall Emmers 42.1%, and no fight on this card depends more completely on a single setting. At that value his profile is essentially the featherweight average and the fight reads Emmers 56.0%. The override sets him to 0.450, and the favorite flips: Douglas goes from 44.0% to 57.9%. The override is not a small adjustment to this projection; it IS this projection.

What the extra weight lets through is a genuinely extreme set of rates. At 0.450 trust Douglas's power composite reads +2.26 — the highest on the card — with an output of +1.55, an early-finish score of 0.931 (also the card's highest), a finishing ability of 1.000 and a raw knockout finish rate of 1.000, off a volume of 8.675 and a strike differential of +3.855. The result is a knockout-threat index of +2.70 against Emmers's +0.36, the widest on the card, and a Douglas knockout at 28.8%. The honest framing is that these are the rates of a man who has spent four minutes in the Octagon and finished both times in round one; a 0.450 trust says take them at roughly half weight, and the model still makes him the favorite.

Emmers is the more complete profile and the one the fight length favors. He owns the decision edge (+0.55), the reach (+1.51, 187.96cm to 182.88cm), the grappling (+0.87 to -0.07), the wrestling defense (+0.85 to +0.19) and 81.3% takedown defense against a man who has never attempted a takedown in the UFC — and a JAMALL EMMERS DECISION at 29.1% is in fact the largest single terminal state in the fight, ahead of Douglas's knockout. What undermines him is durability and mileage: his chin reads -0.66 with a chin-damage factor of 0.679, his getting-finished index is 0.600, he is 37.1 years old with an age factor of 0.872, and he arrives on a 281-day layoff. Note that the published Over 2.5 of 54.5% is not the naive blend — the coherence guardrail lifted it from 46.0% to clear the fight's 53.2% decision rate, the largest such correction on this card.

Padilla also carries the higher divisional Elo, 1828 across five fights to Haqparast's 1775 across fifteen — one of the few fights on this card where the rating and the projection agree against the more experienced man. The trust asymmetry runs the other way, though: Haqparast is at 1.000 on 176 minutes, Padilla at 0.761 on 53.3, so Padilla's advantage is being reported at about three-quarters strength and would widen if you believed his sample outright.

At 95.0% standing time this is the most striking-dominant fight on the card, and Padilla wins that exchange on the model's numbers. His output composite reads +1.03 to Haqparast's +0.49, his reach +1.23 to +0.22 (187.96cm to 182.88cm), his chin +0.45 to -0.85, and his wrestling defense +0.80. Underneath, he lands 47.0% of his head strikes to Haqparast's 40.2% and absorbs 3.003 per minute against a Haqparast figure of 4.057 — the highest absorption rate on this card. That yields a +1.05 knockout-threat index against Haqparast's -0.18, a -0.80 decision edge, and a Padilla decision as the modal outcome at 38.2% with a 21.6% knockout behind it.

The durability comparison is the fight in miniature. Padilla's chin-damage factor is 0.991, his early-vulnerability 0.083 and his getting-finished index 0.000 — he has never been stopped. Haqparast reads 0.740, 0.532 and 0.400, and his most recent outing was a first-round knockout loss to Quillan Salkilld last October, after which he has been out 295 days. What Haqparast retains is real: his wrestling defense composite is the better of the two at +1.21, his takedown defense 86.0%, his effective decision rate 0.727 and his r3-vs-r1 ratio 2.159 — he is a late-rounds fighter who has gone the distance repeatedly, which is what his 19.1% decision share encodes, and 57.3% of sims do reach the judges. Padilla's flags are that his sample is five fights, that his last outing was a majority draw with MarQuel Mederos — who fights earlier on this card as a 20.9% underdog — and that a 0.761 trust means a quarter of his profile is still divisional average.

synopsis.body: Modal outcome is a Padilla decision at 38.2% with a 21.6% knockout; 57.3% of sims reach the judges and 95.0% of fight time is standing — the card's most striking-dominant matchup. He leads on output (+1.03 to +0.49), reach (+1.23 to +0.22) and chin (+0.45 to -0.85), and absorbs 3.003 head strikes per minute against Haqparast's card-high 4.057. Moderate confidence. Against the read: his last outing was a majority draw with MarQuel Mederos, a 20.9% underdog earlier on this card, and Haqparast owns the better wrestling defense (+1.21), 86.0% takedown defense and a 2.159 r3-vs-r1 ratio that make the 19.1% decision path his real one.

matchupAnalysis: Jackson McVey 72.3% / Wes Schultz 27.7%, with the GBM at 75.0% and the hand-tuned model at 58.4%, and the ratings marginally supporting it at 1543 to 1486. This is the least-constrained fight on the card by a clear margin: McVey's computed trust is 0.178 — the lowest of the twenty fighters here — on three UFC fights and 12.45 minutes, and Schultz's is 0.359 on four fights and 25.1 minutes. Roughly four-fifths of McVey's composite profile is the middleweight average, so almost nothing below should be read as a strong claim about either man.

What separates them in the model is durability against a striking profile. McVey's chin reads +0.183 with a chin-damage factor of 1.000 against Schultz's -1.013 and 0.750, and Schultz's early-vulnerability of 0.810 is the highest on the card. McVey also leads on reach (+1.01 to +0.76, 195.58cm apiece by measurement but different frames), output (+0.54 to -0.04) and the underlying striking rates by a wide margin: 63.5% head-strike accuracy — the best on this card — against 34.7%, a volume of 6.506 against 2.908, and a strike differential of +3.133 against -0.199. That produces a +1.23 knockout-threat index against Schultz's -0.14 and a McVey knockout at 33.3%, the modal outcome, with 36.7% of all sims ending in round one.

The honest reading of both records complicates that. Every one of McVey's three UFC fights has ended in a submission — he submitted Sedriques Dumas in round one in April, and was submitted by Zach Reese and by Brunno Ferreira before that — so his finishing ability and getting-finished indices both read 1.000, and his takedown defense is 0.0%. Schultz is the mirror image: both of his UFC wins are submissions, he attempts 0.239 submissions per minute (the highest rate on the card), and his own takedown defense is also 0.0%. So the model's 12.0% Schultz submission share is his single best path and is probably the most under-stated number in this fight — two fighters who have never stopped a takedown, one of whom hunts submissions and one of whom has been submitted twice in three outings. The published Over 2.5 of 41.1% is post-guardrail, lifted from a naive 36.5% to clear the 41.0% decision rate.

synopsis.body: Modal terminal state is a McVey KO/TKO at 33.3%, off a +1.23 knockout-threat index, the card's best head-strike accuracy (63.5% to 34.7%) and a +3.133 strike differential; 36.7% of sims end in round one. Schultz's -1.01 chin and card-high 0.810 early-vulnerability are the target. Lowest confidence on the card. McVey's computed trust is 0.178 — the lowest of these twenty fighters — on three UFC fights and 12.45 minutes, so four-fifths of his profile is divisional average. And the shape may be wrong even if the direction is right: all three of McVey's UFC fights ended in submission (he lost two of them that way), both of Schultz's UFC wins are submissions, Schultz attempts the most submissions per minute on the card, and BOTH men have 0.0% takedown defense. Schultz's 12.0% submission share looks like the most under-priced number here.

matchupAnalysis: Shanelle Dyer 87.4% / Elise Reed 12.6% — the widest projection on the card, with both engines in rare agreement (GBM 87.4%, hand-tuned 88.8%) and the ratings supporting it at 1544 across two division fights to 1454 across nine. The caveat is the familiar one: Dyer's computed trust is 0.304 on two UFC fights and 21.3 minutes, so most of her composite profile is the strawweight average, while Reed sits at full trust on 97.6 minutes. As with the big favorites on recent cards, the number is built far more on what Reed has been measured doing than on what Dyer has demonstrated.

Reed's profile is the most comprehensively negative on the card. Her chin reads -1.78 — the worst here — with a chin-damage factor of 0.613 and a getting-finished index of 1.000; her grappling is -1.06 and her wrestling defense -0.98; her reach composite is -0.41, corresponding to 160.02cm, the shortest on the card; her raw finish rate is 0.000, meaning no stoppage wins in her UFC career at all, against a finishing ability index of 0.000. She is 33.7 years old, her momentum reads -0.452 and her recent-three win rate 0.333, and she arrives on a 456-day layoff — the longest of anyone here — after a round-two knockout loss to Denise Gomes in May 2025. Against that, Dyer's +2.25 knockout-threat index and 1.000 chin-damage factor produce a 53.0% Dyer decision as the modal outcome, with an 18.5% knockout and a 16.0% submission behind it.

Two things deserve to sit alongside the 87.4%. The first is that Reed's own knockout-threat index reads +1.385 — not a small number — because Dyer's chin composite is -1.335 and Dyer's absorption rate is 3.148 head strikes per minute. Reed has one live route, and the model's 2.6% knockout share arguably understates it more than any other number in this fight. The second is that Dyer's measured record is 1-1 in the UFC: a round-two knockout of Ravena Oliveira in March against a decision loss to Carol Foro. Her volume of 7.706 and 100% takedown defense are real and encouraging, and at 25.3 she is eight years younger, but two fights is two fights. Expect a long fight either way — 60.5% of sims reach the judges, and the published Over 2.5 of 62.1% is post-guardrail, lifted from a naive 58.1% to clear that decision rate.

synopsis.body: Modal outcome is a Dyer decision at 53.0% with an 18.5% knockout and 16.0% submission behind it; 60.5% of sims reach the judges. The margin is built on Reed's measured decline — a card-worst -1.78 chin, a 1.000 getting-finished index, -1.06 grappling, -0.98 wrestling defense, a 0.000 career finish rate, a 456-day layoff (the longest here) and a knockout loss to Denise Gomes last time out. Moderate confidence at most despite the size of the number. Dyer is at 0.304 trust on two UFC fights and 21.3 minutes, so this is a verdict on Reed rather than a demonstration by Dyer, and her own record is 1-1. Note Reed's knockout-threat index still reads +1.385 against Dyer's -1.335 chin and 3.148 absorption rate — her 2.6% KO share is the number most likely to be understated.
